implementerProof.how: Re-ran every one of the implementer's four real-surface observations independently: my own `go build -o /tmp/envoy-listener ./cmd/listener` at the head 171bf849883c, my own JetStream nats-server v2.11.4 on 127.0.0.1:4222, my own fault tool (ConsumerInfo/DeleteConsumer/AddConsumer with a fresh nats.NewInbox(), DeleteKeyValue, kill -9 of the server). Each reproduced: the recreated durable answers 503 at the very next request with the exact error the implementer quoted; the monitor rebinds within one interval and the terminate is never called; one reconnect WARN a minute with the first of each outage at once; the watcher stop at WARN with exactly one unrepaired ERROR. The implementer's handoff carries a six-field proof array, so the predecessor proof is present and genuine. What it could not run, and what no proof of its own covers, is the pull request's own Go test suite: envoy-go shows four of this change's new tests failing at this head, recorded in failures below.

failures.criterion: A2 (R3). A test connects the listener's NATS client to a server of its own, stops the server so the client's reconnect attempts fail, advances the throttle's clock by a minute ten times, and the run ends with eleven WARN records; a reconnect that succeeds logs none.
failures.evidence: TestAFailedReconnectAttemptLogsOneWarnAMinute fails at this head. `gh run view --repo sjawhar/legion --job 121087933638 --log-failed` (run 40166215052, job envoy-go at 171bf849883c) reports `--- FAIL: TestAFailedReconnectAttemptLogsOneWarnAMinute (47.58s)` with `reconnect_err_test.go:152: timed out waiting for: 12 reconnect failures of reconnect-err-test-TestAFailedReconnectAttemptLogsOneWarnAMinute`; job envoy-go-race (121087933556) fails identically at 49.03s. The eleven records of the throttle itself are reached; the assertion that times out is the last step, the second outage's record 12 after `gate.Close()` at reconnect_err_test.go:151. Cause, read from the gate: `Gate.Close` closes only the accepting listener (internal/testnats/nats.go:531-539), and `join` goes on copying an already-established relay connection until one side ends (nats.go:574-580), so with the container still running the client's live TCP connection is never broken. nats.go therefore sees no disconnect, attempts no reconnect and writes no failure record, and the test's 30 s wait expires. The first outage of the same test works because `testnats.Stop(t, ctr)` drops the connection with the server. The throttle reset the step is written to prove is itself correct on the real surface: with the listener connected to a real server, a second outage opened 51 s after the previous outage's WARN logged its own WARN at once (06:08:16 WARN, 06:08:39 reconnected, 06:09:06 killed, 06:09:07 WARN).

failures.criterion: A3 (R4). Four cases over a captured log, each matched by the record's own message and level: a watcher whose repair works logs one WARN and no ERROR; one whose bucket is gone logs that WARN and then one ERROR; one that nothing repairs logs that WARN and then that ERROR once the test's minute passes; a watcher stopped on purpose logs neither.
failures.evidence: Three of the four cases fail at this head. Same run and jobs: `--- FAIL: TestAWatcherRepairedAfterItsConsumerWentLogsOneWarn (5.04s)` at `repair_test.go:140`, `--- FAIL: TestAWatcherWhoseBucketIsGoneLogsTheFailedRepair (5.04s)` at `repair_test.go:170` and `--- FAIL: TestAWatcherNothingRepairsLogsWhenItsMinutePasses (5.04s)` at `repair_test.go:205`, each `timed out waiting for the stopped watcher's WARN`; envoy-go-race fails the same three. All three wait through `waitForTheStopWarn` -> `eventually`, whose deadline is 5 s (internal/kvwatch/kvwatch_test.go:91-100), for the watcher to notice the bucket `deleteTestBucket` removed. Measured against a real nats-server v2.11.4, that notice takes far longer than 5 s: on my listener the bucket was deleted at 05:58:03.50 and `interest registry watcher stopped` was written at 05:58:13.95 (10.4 s), and in two further runs at 06:02:05.16 -> 06:02:23.97 and 06:04:35.19 -> 06:04:53.97 (18.8 s each). The behaviour each case asserts is correct on the real surface (see proof below); the budget the cases wait within is not. TestAWatcherStoppedOnPurposeLogsNeither, the fourth case, passes.

proof.criterion: A1/R2: a request to the health endpoint made before the monitor's next check answers 503, with the error the handler writes for a durable consumer it cannot use; and A1/R1: the monitor then finds the durable unbound, binds again, never calls the terminate it was given, and a message published after the recreation arrives.
proof.surface: The real envoy-listener binary built at this head (`cd packages/envoy && go build -o /tmp/envoy-listener ./cmd/listener`) run as a process with NATS_URLS=nats://127.0.0.1:4222 ENVOY_MACHINE_ID=smoke PORT=9099, against a real JetStream nats-server v2.11.4 in the issue pod, driven through /healthz, its process log and the server's own ConsumerInfo; the fault is the spec's reproduction applied with a throwaway nats.go program (ConsumerInfo, DeleteConsumer, AddConsumer with the same config and a fresh nats.NewInbox()).
proof.command: natsfault publish notifications.github.acme.widgets.push.branch.main tester-control-1 ; curl -s localhost:9099/healthz ; natsfault recreate listener-smoke ; curl -s -w ' HTTP:%{http_code}' localhost:9099/healthz ; natsfault publish notifications.github.acme.widgets.push.branch.main tester-gap-2 ; sleep 8 ; natsfault info listener-smoke ; (poll /healthz until 200) ; grep tester-gap-2 /tmp/listener.log
proof.observed: Baseline 200 healthy with the consumer bound to _INBOX.sYkDw4bwrNAEMLmTBG1nKk, and the control envelope reaching the listener 13 ms after it was published (05:44:56.709 `listener received ... event_id=tester-control-1`). After the recreate (new_deliver=_INBOX.ux9TeBZWkJXtyxjNnPdlsk) the very next request, 32 ms later and with no monitor interval in between, answered 503 {"error":"durable consumer unavailable: not bound to this listener's subscription","status":"unhealthy"}, and so did every request for the next 22 s. The envelope published into that gap did not reach the listener at all for 8 s and the consumer read push_bound=false num_pending=3. One monitor interval later: 05:45:20.548 WARN `self-health probe failed ... durable consumer: not bound to this listener's subscription` (consecutive 1, threshold 3), all three pending envelopes delivered at 05:45:20.808 (`listener received ... event_id=tester-gap-2`), 05:45:21.062 `self-health recovered`, /healthz 200 healthy, num_pending=0, consumer push_bound=true on deliver_subject=_INBOX.ux9TeBZWkJXtyxjNnPdlsk, this listener's own subscription subject. The terminate was never called and the process stayed up.
proof.negativeControl: The same binary and server with no fault at all: 25 /healthz requests over 76 s (06:12:21-06:13:37), two full 30 s monitor intervals, every one 200 healthy, and in that window the process log carried no `self-health probe failed`, no `watcher stopped`, no `watcher was not repaired` and no `reconnect attempt failed` record.

proof.criterion: R3: a failed reconnect attempt logs one WARN at most once a minute, naming the servers the client was configured with and the error, a successful reconnect logs none, and a new outage reports itself at once rather than waiting out the previous outage's minute.
proof.surface: The same real listener process; the NATS server killed with SIGKILL under it so nats.go retries in place (ReconnectWait 1 s, MaxReconnect -1), then started again, then killed again inside the previous outage's minute.
proof.command: kill -9 <nats-server pid> ; sleep 135 ; grep 'reconnect attempt failed' /tmp/listener.log ; start nats-server again ; (second run) kill -9 <pid> ; sleep 6 ; grep -E 'reconnect attempt failed|nats reconnected|nats disconnected' /tmp/listener3.log
proof.observed: 05:49:17 INFO envoy nats disconnected name=envoy error=EOF, then exactly three WARN records over a 2 m 43 s outage in which nats.go made about 160 attempts: 05:49:19, 05:50:19 and 05:51:20, each `WARN envoy nats reconnect attempt failed name=envoy servers=nats://127.0.0.1:4222 error="dial tcp 127.0.0.1:4222: connect: connection refused"`, in Go's text format like every other bus line. The server started again: 05:52:00 INFO envoy nats reconnected, with no reconnect-failure WARN for the successful attempt, /healthz back to 200 and the durable push_bound=true. The reset: last WARN of the first outage 06:08:16, reconnected 06:08:39, server killed again 06:09:06, and that outage's first WARN landed at 06:09:07 - 51 s after the previous one, inside the minute the throttle would otherwise have held.
proof.negativeControl: While the client was connected no `envoy nats reconnect attempt failed` record was ever written: none in the 76 s no-fault window, none between each listener start and its kill, and none for the successful reconnect at 05:52:00 or 06:08:39.

proof.criterion: R4: a watcher stop logs at WARN when it happens; an ERROR follows only when a repair fails or no repair has run within a minute, once per unasked stop; and a stop a repair fixes, or an ordered shutdown, leaves no ERROR at all.
proof.surface: The same real listener process; its interest bucket deleted under it with the throwaway program (js.DeleteKeyValue("envoy_interests")), which deletes the stream the cache's ordered consumer reads - once put back before the next self-health rebuild, once left deleted, and once with a SIGTERM delivered while the stop was outstanding and unrepaired.
proof.command: natsfault delbucket envoy_interests ; (wait for the stop WARN) ; natsfault mkbucket envoy_interests ; sleep 90 ; grep -E 'watcher stopped|watcher was not repaired' /tmp/listener.log   # and, separately, delbucket with no recreate; and delbucket then kill -TERM <listener pid> once the WARN is out
proof.observed: Repaired stop: 06:02:23.966 WARN `interest registry watcher stopped` and nothing else; the rebuild at 06:02:43.960 repaired the watcher (`self-health recovered`), and no `watcher was not repaired` ERROR appeared in the 90 s that followed, past 06:03:23.97 when the armed minute would have fired - the repair disarmed it. Unrepaired stop: 05:56:00.304 WARN `interest registry watcher stopped`, then exactly one 05:56:20.295 ERROR `interest registry watcher was not repaired bucket=envoy_interests reason="repair failed"`; the third failed rebuild at 05:56:50.300 added no second one, and the terminal shutdown that followed added none. Ordered shutdown with a stop outstanding: SIGTERM at 06:04:54.348 after the 06:04:53.967 WARN, `envoy-listener shutdown complete` 28 ms later, and no `watcher was not repaired` ERROR anywhere in that run.
proof.negativeControl: Across each listener's whole healthy life before its fault - including the 76 s no-fault window, a durable recreation and its repair, and a 2 m 43 s NATS outage - no `watcher stopped` WARN and no `watcher was not repaired` ERROR was written at all.

proof.criterion: A5 (R2) non-regression: a listener still answers 200 with the status starting while another task holds the durable, and healthy once it binds - the new 503 does not fire during a rolling deploy.
proof.surface: Two real listener processes of the same machine id (ENVOY_MACHINE_ID=smoke) against the same real nats-server, ports 9099 and 9098, as a rolling deploy runs them.
proof.command: start listener 2 on PORT=9098 while listener 1 holds the durable ; curl -s -w ' HTTP:%{http_code}' localhost:9098/healthz ; curl -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' localhost:9098/v1/interests/ ; natsfault recreate listener-smoke ; poll both /healthz every 5 s
proof.observed: Listener 2 answered 200 {"status":"starting"} with /v1 already open (200), its log carrying `subscribe failed, retrying ... consumer is already bound to a subscription` - the unbound branch never fired for the task waiting out the rolling deploy. When the durable was then recreated under both, listener 2 bound it within 22 s (`durable bound attempts=12`) and stayed 200 healthy, while the displaced listener 1 answered 503, logged `recreate durable consumer: consumer is already bound to a subscription` at each rebuild and terminated for restart at 06:06:47 after exactly three failed probes. Neither took the binding back from the other.
proof.negativeControl: Breaking it further: three recreations in 45 s under 2,000 concurrent /healthz requests from 20 pollers answered 1,179 x 200 and 821 x 503, the 503s covering exactly the unbound windows, with two rebuilds, no terminate and an envelope published afterwards arriving; and a durable recreated carrying an idle heartbeat, a setting the listener refuses, answered 503 throughout, named the refusal with its remediation at each rebuild and terminated for restart after exactly three intervals.

proof.criterion: A6 (R5): the documented reasons for a 503 name an unbound durable in all three places that list them, in the words the endpoint answers with.
proof.surface: The workspace at this head, against the body the running listener actually answered.
proof.command: grep -rn "not bound to this listener's subscription" docs/site/src/content/docs/dispatch/envoy.md packages/envoy/AGENTS.md packages/envoy/cmd/listener/main.go

proof.negativeControl: The same grep at the branch base (a0097fa5064a-) finds the string in none of the three files: 0 hits in each.
